interpretation_notes: DEVELOPMENT RUN unless the experiment id is exp-h22-001 produced by the orchestrator in an isolated worktree.
Gate-closed state: the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE by the preregistered domain gate; context numbers are not a trend and feed no support/reject clause.
Slope-uncertainty rule (this evaluator's reading of 'spans both regions'): CI lower bound <= 0.75 and upper bound >= 0.90.
R1 'baseline has equal/lower marginal slope' is read as slope ratio >= 1.0.

inconclusive_if.clause: Fewer than 3 real domains, fewer than 30 completed blind tasks, or the slope uncertainty spans both the support (<= 0.75) and reject (>= 0.90) regions

invalid_if.clause: Task corpus, cost metric or baseline capability changed after reveal
Cost accounting is asymmetric: one variant's equivalent glue / recurring tax is not counted (per-task components or the H18 context snapshot)
Evidence records carry a protocol-freeze / ENGINE_PREREG hash different from the files now
Evidence records disagree on commit / seed / corpus hash

reject_if.clause: With >= 3 real domains and >= 30 tasks: all preregistered task classes have ratio >= 0.90, or the baseline has equal/lower marginal slope (ratio >= 1.0)
With the gate open: apparent savings disappear under fair baseline tooling or require a correctness/security regression

support_if.clause: At least 3 independently useful real domains are included
For >= 2 independent preregistered task classes, median normalized adaptation effort <= 0.75 of baseline with correctness/security non-inferior
Overall marginal adaptation-cost slope across real domains <= 0.75 of baseline slope, with uncertainty reported
A realistic workload tier exists where measured gains are not dominated by recurring ontology tax
